```{r, echo=F}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(GGally)
library(ggcorrplot)

library(qmap) # quantile mapping

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size=16))
```

The anchovy growth model was fitted to temperature data from National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)
Optimum interpolation 0.25° daily sea surface temperature analysis (oiSST version 2.1). Data were averaged in bottom depths
below 500 m based on GEBCO Compilation Group (2022) bathymetry data, within the quadrangle defined by the coordinates 6ºW
43ºN and 0ºW 47ºN.

For the FLBEIA simulations we need temperature data under RCP scenarios. The available data are from POLCOMS-ERSEM (RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5) and NEMO-MEDUSA (RCP 8.5). The POLCOMS-ERSME data were sent by Morgane Travers for the reanalysis period and downloaded from [here](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/cdsapp#!/dataset/sis-marine-properties?tab=overview) for the projection period under the two carbon emission scenarios. The NEMO-MEDUSA data were provided by Jack Maverick and Michael Heath. 

The bias correction was based on the tutorial by Bernhard Kuehn [here](https://figshare.com/articles/software/Tutorial_-_Ways_to_bias_correct_climate_projections/23514618), but was applied to the whole time series, without taking into account the monthly and spatial dimension of the original data. This assumption

```{r}
# environmental data from ORAS5: 1958-2022

oras <- readRDS("C:/Use/GitHub/ices-tools-dev/SEAwise/SEAwise_T3.3/data/env/ORAS5_AnnualTEMPByDemPelStock2.RDS")

ggplot(oras, aes(year, oras5))+

doisst <- readRDS(file.path("env_data_fernando","doisst.rds"))
doisst$tosa = with( doisst, ( tosWinter + tosSpring + tosSummer + tosAutumn ) / 4.0 )
doisst = doisst[ c( 'y', 'tosa' ) ]
names(doisst) <- c("year","oisst")

ggplot(doisst, aes(year, oisst))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  geom_smooth(method="lm", col="grey")

# environmental data from NEMO-MEDUSA: 1980-2099 (RCP 8.5)

aux <- load("C:/Use/proyectos/IM-21-SEAWISE/wp3/env_nemomedusa/NM_series.RData") 
nemomed <- get(aux[[1]])
rm(aux)

nemomed <- subset(nemomed, select=c("Year", "Quarter","YQ","Strata","T0")) %>% 
  filter(Strata %in% c("8.a","8.b","8.c","8.d","8.e")) %>% 
  mutate(Year=as.numeric(Year),
         Quarter=as.numeric(Quarter))

ggplot(nemomed, aes(YQ, T0, group=Strata, col=Strata))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point()+
  facet_grid(~Strata)+
  geom_smooth(method="lm", col="grey")

nemomed <- nemomed %>% 
  group_by(Year) %>% 
  summarise(T0=mean(T0)) %>% 
  rename(year=Year,
         nm85=T0)

ggplot(nemomed, aes(year, nm85))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  geom_smooth(method="lm", col="grey")

# environmental data from NEMO-MEDUSA: 1980-2099 (RCP 8.5)

polcoms.rcp45 <- readRDS("C:/Use/proyectos/IM-21-SEAWISE/wp3/env_polcoms_ersem_sst_proj/POLCOMS_sst_spt45.RDS")
polcoms.rcp45 <- as.data.frame(polcoms.rcp45)
names(polcoms.rcp45) <- c("year","pe45")
polcoms.rcp45$pe45 <- as.numeric(polcoms.rcp45$pe45)

polcoms.rcp85 <- readRDS("C:/Use/proyectos/IM-21-SEAWISE/wp3/env_polcoms_ersem_sst_proj/POLCOMS_sst_spt85.RDS")
polcoms.rcp85 <- as.data.frame(polcoms.rcp85)
names(polcoms.rcp85) <- c("year","pe85")
polcoms.rcp85$pe85 <- as.numeric(polcoms.rcp85$pe85)

# check year ranges without NA's

range(doisst$year[!is.na(doisst$oisst)])
range(oras$year[!is.na(oras$oras5)])
range(nemomed$year[!is.na(nemomed$nm85)])
range(polcoms.rcp45$year[!is.na(polcoms.rcp45$pe45)])
range(polcoms.rcp85$year[!is.na(polcoms.rcp85$pe85)])

# merge all the temperatures, remove 1981 (missing oisst)

temp.dat <- merge(doisst, oras, by="year", all=T)
temp.dat <- merge(temp.dat, nemomed, by="year", all=T)
temp.dat <- merge(temp.dat, polcoms.rcp45, by="year", all=T)
temp.dat <- merge(temp.dat, polcoms.rcp85, by="year", all=T)
temp.dat <- subset(temp.dat, year>=1980) # remove past oras data 

```

```{r, eval=T}

# long format for ggplot plotting

temp.datl <- pivot_longer(temp.dat, cols=c("oras5","oisst","nm85","pe45","pe85"), names_to="source")

ggplot(temp.datl, aes(year, value, col=source, group=source))+
  geom_point()+

  ylab("Temperature (ºC)")+
  xlab("")

ggpairs(temp.dat[, -1]) 

mat <- cor(temp.dat[, -1], use="complete.obs") 
p.mat <- cor_pmat(temp.dat[, -1])
ggcorrplot(mat, type = "lower", lab=T, p.mat = p.mat)

```

# NEMO-MEDUSA

## Delta-method

The mean-bias correction or delta method was applied to the annual time series (not by grid-cell or by month). We use as overlap the most recent overlapping period between oisst and nemo-medusa (1982-2021).

```{r}

# overlapping period

commonyrs <- intersect(doisst$year[!is.na(doisst$oisst)] , nemomed$year[!is.na(nemomed$nm85)])
commonyrs

# calculate bias
bias <- mean(temp.dat$nm85[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]) - mean(temp.dat$oisst[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]) # equivalent to mean(temp.dat$nm85 -temp.dat$oisst)
bias

ggplot(temp.dat, aes(year, nm85-oisst)) + 
  geom_line()+
  geom_point()+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, lty=2)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=bias, col=2)+
  geom_smooth(method="lm", col="grey")

# correct time series

temp.dat$nm85.bias.rm <- temp.dat$nm85 - bias
nemomed$nm85.bias.rm <- nemomed$nm85 - bias

# plots

plot(nemomed$year, nemomed$nm85.bias.rm, type="o", pch=19, col=4, xlab="", ylab="Temperature (ºC)")
lines(nemomed$year, nemomed$nm85, type="o", pch=19, col=3)
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$oisst, type="o", pch=19, col=1)
legend("topleft", c("OISST","NM RCP8.5","NM RCP8.5 bias corr"), lty=1, pch=19, col=c(1,3,4))

```

# Quantile mapping method

Following the steps suggested in the tutorial:

1. decide on a time period to base the quantile mapping on - aka the ‘correction time period’ (normally the mutually overlapping period between historical data and projections, e.g. 2006 - 2020 or overlap between historical part and a control run)
2. remove the individual trends from both the historical part and projection in this ‘correction time period’
3. perform Quantile mapping on this trend-corrected data
4. remove the trend from the whole projection period (e.g. 2006 - 2100)
5. apply this fitted Qmap-model to this trend corrected data for the whole projection period
6. calculate the mean-bias (same as for the delta correction method above) for the chosen ‘correction time period’
add everything back together: the qmapped-projection - the mean bias + the projection trend

For step 2 and 3, one could use also the trend corrected data of the whole projection period and skip step 4. 

```{r}
# overlapping period

commonyrs <- intersect(doisst$year[!is.na(doisst$oisst)] , nemomed$year[!is.na(nemomed$nm85)])
commonyrs

# detrend the past time series

m.oisst <- lm(oisst ~ year, data=temp.dat)
m.nm <- lm(nm85 ~ year, data=nemomed) # detrend the whole time series

temp.dat$oisst.detrend <- temp.dat$oisst - predict(m.oisst)
temp.dat$nm85.detrend <- temp.dat$nm85 - predict(m.nm, newdata=temp.dat)
nemomed$nm85.detrend <- nemomed$nm85 - predict(m.nm)

# bias (same as above)
bias <- mean(temp.dat$nm85[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]) - mean(temp.dat$oisst[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]) 

# quantile mapping on detrended data

plot(ecdf(temp.dat$oisst.detrend[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]), verticals=T)
lines(ecdf(temp.dat$nm85.detrend[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]), col=2, verticals=T)

# fitQmap identifyes the parameters of different quantile mapping methods
# doQmap performs quantile mapping using previously defined parameters

qmap <- fitQmap(obs = temp.dat$oisst.detrend[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs],
               mod = temp.dat$nm85.detrend[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs],
               method = "RQUANT",
               wet.day = F)
out <- doQmap(x = nemomed$nm85.detrend, fobj = qmap, type = "linear2") 

# reconstruct series
nemomed$nm85.qmap <- out - bias + predict(m.nm, data=nemomed)
temp.dat$nm85.qmap <- nemomed$nm85.qmap[match(temp.dat$year, nemomed$year)]

# plot

plot(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$nm85.qmap, type="o", pch=19, col=2, xlab="", ylab="Temperature (ºC)")
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$nm85, type="o", pch=19, col=3)
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$oisst, type="o", pch=19, col=1)
legend("topleft", c("OISST","NM RCP 8.5","NM RCP 8.5 qmap"), lty=1, pch=19, col=c(1,3,2))
```

## Comparison of the two bias correction methods

In this case both methods give similar results:

```{r}
plot(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$nm85.qmap, type="o", pch=19, col=2, xlab="", ylab="Temperature (ºC)")
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$nm85, type="o", pch=19, col=3)
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$nm85.bias.rm, type="o", pch=19, col=4)
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$oisst, type="o", pch=19, col=1)
legend("topleft", c("OISST","NM RCP 8.5","NM RCP 8.5 bias corr","NM RCP 8.5 qmap"), lty=1, pch=19, col=c(1,3,4,2))
```

# POLCOMS-ERSEM RCP 4.5

## Delta-method

The mean-bias correction or delta method was applied to the annual time series (not by grid-cell or by month). We use as overlap the most recent overlapping period between oisst and polcoms (2006-2021).

```{r}

# overlapping period

commonyrs <- intersect(doisst$year[!is.na(doisst$oisst)] , polcoms.rcp45$year[!is.na(polcoms.rcp45$pe45)])
commonyrs

# calculate bias
bias <- mean(temp.dat$pe45[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]) - mean(temp.dat$oisst[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]) 
bias

ggplot(temp.dat, aes(year, pe45-oisst)) + 
  geom_line()+
  geom_point()+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, lty=2)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=bias, col=2)+
  geom_smooth(method="lm", col="grey")

# correct time series

temp.dat$pe45.bias.rm <- temp.dat$pe45 - bias
polcoms.rcp45$pe45.bias.rm <- polcoms.rcp45$pe45 - bias

# plots

plot(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$pe45.bias.rm, type="o", pch=19, col=4, xlab="", ylab="Temperature (ºC)")
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$pe45, type="o", pch=19, col=3)
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$oisst, type="o", pch=19, col=1)
legend("topleft", c("OISST","PE RCP4.5","PE RCP4.5 bias corr"), lty=1, pch=19, col=c(1,3,4))

```

# Quantile mapping method

Following the steps suggested in the tutorial as before for NEMO-MEDUSA data. 

```{r}
# overlapping period

commonyrs <- intersect(doisst$year[!is.na(doisst$oisst)] , polcoms.rcp45$year[!is.na(polcoms.rcp45$pe45)])
commonyrs

# detrend the past time series

m.oisst <- lm(oisst ~ year, data=temp.dat)
m.pe45 <- lm(pe45 ~ year, data=polcoms.rcp45) # detrend the whole time series

temp.dat$oisst.detrend <- temp.dat$oisst - predict(m.oisst)
temp.dat$pe45.detrend <- temp.dat$pe45 - predict(m.pe45, newdata=temp.dat)
polcoms.rcp45$pe45.detrend <- polcoms.rcp45$pe45 - predict(m.pe45)

# bias (same as above)
bias <- mean(temp.dat$pe45[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]) - mean(temp.dat$oisst[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]) 
bias

# quantile mapping on detrended data

plot(ecdf(temp.dat$oisst.detrend[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]), verticals=T)
lines(ecdf(temp.dat$pe45.detrend[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs]), col=2, verticals=T)

# fitQmap identifyes the parameters of different quantile mapping methods
# doQmap performs quantile mapping using previously defined parameters

qmap <- fitQmap(obs = temp.dat$oisst.detrend[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs],
               mod = temp.dat$pe45.detrend[temp.dat$year %in% commonyrs],
               method = "RQUANT",
               wet.day = F)
out <- doQmap(x = polcoms.rcp45$pe45.detrend, fobj = qmap, type = "linear2") 

# reconstruct series
polcoms.rcp45$pe45.qmap <- out - bias + predict(m.pe45, data=polcoms.rcp45)
temp.dat$pe45.qmap <- polcoms.rcp45$pe45.qmap[match(temp.dat$year, polcoms.rcp45$year)]

# plot

plot(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$pe45.qmap, type="o", pch=19, col=2, xlab="", ylab="Temperature (ºC)")
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$pe45, type="o", pch=19, col=3)
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$oisst, type="o", pch=19, col=1)
legend("topleft", c("OISST","PE RCP 4.5","PE RCP 4.5 qmap"), lty=1, pch=19, col=c(1,3,2))
```

## Comparison of the two bias correction methods

In this case both methods give similar results:

```{r}
plot(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$pe45.qmap, type="o", pch=19, col=2, xlab="", ylab="Temperature (ºC)")
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$pe45, type="o", pch=19, col=3)
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$pe45.bias.rm, type="o", pch=19, col=4)
lines(temp.dat$year, temp.dat$oisst, type="o", pch=19, col=1)
legend("topleft", c("OISST","PE RCP 4.5","PE RCP 4.5 bias corr","PE RCP 4.5 qmap"), lty=1, pch=19, col=c(1,3,4,2))
```
